name: Bollinger Bands
description: Bollinger Bands consist of a middle band (20-period SMA), an upper band (middle + 2 standard deviations), and a lower band (middle - 2 standard deviations). They adapt to volatility: bands widen during high volatility and narrow during low volatility. Approximately 95% of price action occurs within the bands under normal conditions. Bollinger Bands are used to identify volatility regimes, potential breakouts, mean reversion setups, and trend strength via band walking.

signals.condition: Bollinger Band Squeeze: bands are at their narrowest in recent history (bandwidth at multi-period low)
signals.interpretation: Low volatility compression phase; a significant directional breakout is building; direction undetermined until breakout candle; watch for volume confirmation

signals.condition: Price breaks out of squeeze with strong candle and volume
signals.interpretation: Volatility expansion beginning; breakout direction is the likely trend direction; do not fade the initial breakout bar

signals.condition: Price walks along or repeatedly touches the upper band
signals.interpretation: Strong uptrend in progress; band walking is a sign of trend strength, not overbought; do not short just because price is at upper band

signals.condition: Price walks along or repeatedly touches the lower band
signals.interpretation: Strong downtrend in progress; band walking is a sign of trend weakness, not oversold; do not buy just because price is at lower band

signals.condition: Price touches lower band in a ranging market with middle band flat
signals.interpretation: Mean reversion long opportunity; look for bullish candlestick confirmation before entry

signals.condition: Price touches upper band in a ranging market with middle band flat
signals.interpretation: Mean reversion short opportunity; look for bearish candlestick confirmation before entry

signals.condition: Price closes outside upper band then returns inside
signals.interpretation: Potential reversal or exhaustion of upward move; watch for follow-through sell on the next bar

signals.condition: Price closes outside lower band then returns inside
signals.interpretation: Potential reversal or exhaustion of downward move; watch for follow-through buy on the next bar
Extremely extended to the upside; in ranging markets this signals high reversal probability; in trends this is normal band walk
Extremely extended to the downside; in ranging markets this signals high reversal probability; in trends this is normal band walk
Price reclaiming the middle band from below; bullish momentum shift; potential long entry in trending context
Price losing the middle band from above; bearish momentum shift; potential short entry in trending context

signals.condition: Bands widening rapidly after a period of contraction
signals.interpretation: Volatility expansion confirmed; the squeeze has resolved; momentum in breakout direction is real

rules.rule: Never use band touches alone as buy or sell signals. First determine if the market is trending or ranging using the slope of the middle band and price structure.
rules.rationale: Band touches in a trend (band walking) are continuation signals, not reversal signals. Treating them as reversals leads to trading against the trend.

rules.rule: In a ranging market (flat middle band), use lower band touches as long setups and upper band touches as short setups. Require a confirming candlestick reversal pattern before entry.
rules.rationale: Mean reversion to the middle band works in ranges but not in trends. The confirming candle reduces false entries when a range is breaking down.

rules.rule: In a trending market (sloping middle band), trade band touches in the trend direction only. A touch of the lower band in an uptrend is a pullback entry opportunity, not a short signal.
rules.rationale: Trends frequently see price pull back to the lower band without reversing. These pullbacks offer low-risk trend continuation entries.

rules.rule: Monitor bandwidth (upper band minus lower band) for squeeze identification. When bandwidth falls to the lowest level in 20 or more bars, classify as a squeeze and watch for breakout.
rules.rationale: Volatility is cyclical. Extended periods of contraction reliably precede expansion. Squeeze identification gives early warning of impending large moves.

rules.rule: Do not predict breakout direction from a squeeze. Wait for price and volume to confirm the direction. The first strong candle with expanding volume determines the breakout direction.
rules.rationale: Squeezes resolve in either direction. Anticipating direction without confirmation leads to 50/50 trades with poor setup quality.

rules.rule: Use %B indicator to normalize price position within the bands. %B below 0.2 in a range = buy zone; %B above 0.8 in a range = sell zone. Middle band (%B = 0.5) is the mean reversion target.
rules.rationale: %B translates band position into a 0-1 scale that is easier to compare across instruments and time frames.

rules.rule: Combine Bollinger Bands with RSI or volume indicators. A lower band touch with RSI divergence and decreasing sell volume is a high-probability mean reversion long setup.
rules.rationale: Bollinger Bands identify the location of price relative to volatility boundaries; momentum and volume indicators confirm whether reversal pressure is actually building.

agent_use: Use Bollinger Bands to classify volatility regime and identify setup type. First assess middle band slope: flat = range mode, sloping = trend mode. In range mode: flag lower band touches as mean reversion long candidates and upper band touches as mean reversion short candidates; require confirming candlestick. In trend mode: flag band touches in the trend direction as continuation entries; flag band touches against trend as caution. Calculate bandwidth and flag squeeze (bandwidth at 20-bar low) as a pre-breakout alert. Report %B value, bandwidth status (squeeze/normal/expanded), middle band slope direction, and setup classification (mean_reversion/trend_continuation/squeeze_alert) in every analysis output.
